\section{Prior art and the published lower-bound conflict}
\label{qua:sec:prior-art}

Previous quantum papers under the phrase ``Ramsey algorithm'' solve different
problems.  Gaitan and Clark encode the existence of avoidance colourings in
an adiabatic Hamiltonian \cite{GaitanClark2012}; Wang searches the space of
$2^{\binom V2}$ labelled graphs when testing a Ramsey threshold
\cite{Wang2016}; and Pion and Mniszewski study QUBO reduction and quantum
annealing for bound discovery \cite{PionMniszewski2025}.  Their square roots
refer to the number of graph colourings, not the number of vertices of one
given graph.  D{"o}rn's clique and independent-set query algorithms are
closer in oracle model but do not exploit the Ramsey totality promise or the
majority recursion \cite{Doern2005}.  To our knowledge, no earlier work uses
implicit-set quantum sampling to implement the constructive
Erdős--Szekeres proof.  Because the construction is elementary, this remains
a priority claim requiring expert confirmation rather than an asserted
exhaustive fact.

The closest exact-model source is Jain--Li--Robere--Xun
\cite{JainLiRobereXun2024}.  Their formal Definition~2.6 has $N=2^n$
vertices, and the sentence immediately following Definition~2.7 declares
the default target to be $K=n/2$.  (Their introductory shorthand instead
prints $N=2^{n+1}$ and target $n$; we do not use that internally inconsistent
sentence for the parameter comparison.)  Their query-complexity paragraph
states a quantum lower
bound $N^{1-o(1)}$, citing their graph-hash reduction and the
Liu--Zhandry multi-collision lower bound \cite{LiuZhandry2019}.  The reduction
produces symmetric valid graph instances, so the invalid-encoding escape
clause does not resolve the conflict with \cref{qua:cor:succinct}.  Independently,
\cref{qua:cor:unpromised} aligns the upper bound with the full locally verifiable
relation by canonicalizing an arbitrary adjacency circuit and checking only
the returned witness.

Here is the direct parameter calculation.  Let $B$ be the collision range
size and $t$ the fixed collision multiplicity.  The reduction uses a Ramsey
host of size $M\asymp B^{4t}$.  Liu--Zhandry's exponent in $B$ is
\[
 \alpha_t=\frac{2^{t-1}-1}{2^t-1}.
\]
The inherited exponent in $M$ is therefore
\[
 \frac{\alpha_t}{4t}.
\]
It equals $1/24$ at $t=2$; for $t\ge3$ it is less than
$1/(8t)\le1/24$.  Thus the two cited ingredients yield a nontrivial
$\Omega(M^{1/24})$ lower bound, subject to the reduction's rounding and
promise conventions, but do not yield $M^{1-o(1)}$.

The upper theorem and the printed near-linear lower cannot both hold in the
same promised valid-graph query model.  We have found no public correction in
a targeted forward-citation search.  We record the calculation so that the
logical boundary is visible; author clarification remains required before
submission, and no claim about the source authors' intended parameterization
is made here.
